name: LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS ReMotion Voluntary Motor Restoration
description:
The LAZARUS ReMotion is a voluntary motor restoration BCI designed for patients with acquired or congenital motor pathway disruption, including spinal cord injury, ALS-spectrum motor neuron disease, stroke-related motor deficit, and limb-loss requiring prosthetic neural integration. The device deploys a 1,024-electrode primary motor cortex and supplementary motor area array, capturing motor intent signals upstream of the point of pathway failure and routing them via encrypted low-latency wireless transmission to peripheral effector systems — prosthetic limbs, exoskeletal assistive devices, functional electrical stimulation arrays in partially innervated musculature, or robotic mobility platforms. The ReMotion's signal processing pipeline uses a patient-specific movement decoder trained over a 45-day calibration period, achieving sub-50ms intent-to-actuation latency in clinical conditions and maintaining functional performance in high-interference urban electromagnetic environments through a proprietary frequency-hopping transmission protocol. The device also includes a proprioceptive feedback return channel, allowing compatible prosthetic and assistive hardware to deliver simulated tactile and positional sensation back to the somatosensory cortex, substantially improving the naturalism and precision of motor control compared to open-loop systems.

For the hundreds of thousands of GLMZ residents living with motor disabilities — a population swelled by industrial accidents in the city's lower manufacturing sectors, combat injuries among veterans who served in corporate conflicts, and the ongoing legacy of a toxic contamination event in the outer eastern corridors that caused a spike in neurodegenerative motor disease — the ReMotion represents genuine liberation. LAZARUS has made a deliberate commercial decision to position the device as a medical necessity rather than an elective enhancement, qualifying it for GLMZ's Elder and Disability Augmentation Subsidy Program and maintaining a licensed price point that, while still substantial, is within reach of middle-tier incomes. The gap between the subsidized and unsubsidized populations remains stark, however — outer corridor residents who cannot qualify for the subsidy due to documentation requirements face a Φ9,500 street-price alternative through gray market installers, with all the quality control and rejection risk that entails.
legality: Unrestricted (Medical) — prescription required from licensed neurologist or rehabilitation specialist; covered under GLMZ Disability Augmentation Subsidy Program (income and documentation qualified)
installation_requirements: Licensed neurosurgeon with motor cortex mapping specialization; 45-day pre-installation motor intent baseline mapping; peripheral effector system compatibility assessment; rehabilitation program enrollment recommended post-installation
rejection_risk: Low-moderate (7.1% overall; elevated to 12% in patients with significant motor cortex scarring from prior injury)
maintenance: Monthly movement decoder refinement (OTA); quarterly electrode impedance check; annual full system review; proprioceptive feedback calibration as peripheral hardware changes
specifications: {"motor_cortex_electrodes": 1024, "sma_electrodes": 256, "intent_capture_regions": ["primary motor cortex", "supplementary motor area"], "signal_latency": "<50 ms (clinical conditions)", "transmission_protocol": "frequency-hopping encrypted wireless", "compatible_effectors": ["prosthetic limbs", "exoskeletal assistive devices", "FES arrays", "robotic mobility platforms"], "calibration_period": "45 days", "proprioceptive_feedback": "yes (somatosensory cortex return channel)", "battery_life": "20 months (inductive recharge)", "movement_decoder": "patient-specific, OTA-refinable", "subsidy_program": "GLMZ DASP qualified"}
side_effects: Phantom limb phenomenon modification — patients with limb loss report that proprioceptive feedback from prosthetics can create vivid phantom sensations of the original limb rather than the prosthetic, causing spatial disorientation during early use

Motor overflow in 5% of users: the device occasionally captures and transmits incidental motor planning activity (imagined movements, involuntary preparation signals) causing minor unintended prosthetic or effector movements

Psychological adjustment period of 3–6 months during which patients report identity dissonance between self-image and newly restored motor capability; LAZARUS recommends concurrent psychological support
cultural_context: LAZARUS has worked hard to embed the ReMotion within GLMZ's disability advocacy community, sponsoring rehabilitation centers, funding user collectives, and maintaining a patient support network that has become genuinely influential as a political constituency. ReMotion users are among the most organized and vocal advocates for augmentation subsidy expansion in the city's civic governance structures. In the outer corridors, however, the subsidy program's documentation requirements effectively exclude many of the residents who most need the device — undocumented workers, refugees, and those whose disabilities were caused by corporate activities that were never formally acknowledged — creating a parallel gray market installation ecosystem that LAZARUS officially condemns and unofficially tolerates.
known_users: Veterans of corporate-sponsored armed conflicts using the device for combat-injury motor restoration
Industrial accident survivors from GLMZ's lower manufacturing and extraction sectors
Patients with ALS-spectrum and other progressive motor neuron diseases in LAZARUS-partnered care facilities
Outer corridor residents using gray market installations due to subsidy documentation barriers
story_hooks: A ReMotion patient's device begins capturing and transmitting not just motor intent signals but fragments of what appear to be higher-order planning cognition — tactical movement sequences, spatial memory of locations she has never visited, behavioral patterns that don't match her profile. Her neurologist suspects her device was quietly enrolled in an undisclosed research protocol without her consent.

The gray market installer network serving undocumented outer corridor residents is using a batch of ReMotion units that have been modified with a secondary telemetry module. Someone is building a database of motor-disabled individuals in the outer corridors — their identities, locations, and physical capabilities. The purpose is unclear but the implications for a vulnerable population are severe.

A LAZARUS rehabilitation center is offering experimental ReMotion installations to patients with progressive motor neuron disease at no cost — but the consent forms buried in the documentation include rights to post-mortem neural data. A patient's family wants to know what LAZARUS is actually building with decades of dying patients' motor cortex recordings.
